title: kate-core: count the folds that cover an offset
summary: View::fold_covering_count returns how many stored ranges contain the offset. The end offset counts as zero. The test goes in the existing view tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: view.rs has one test module named tests.  Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not add a second module with the same name. Add fold_covering_count on View. Return the count of self.folds whose contains method is true for at. Do not touch apply_indent_folds, offset_is_folded, folded_range_at, char_range_for_span, header_line_break, or line_scalar. The test fold_covering_count_counts_every_range builds a view the same way as the_header_text_is_outside_the_fold. apply_indent_folds of a, newline, two spaces, b, newline, and tab width 4. Offset 0 returns 0. Offset 1 returns 1. Offset 5 returns 1. Offset 6 returns 0. Then assign folds to 0..10 and 2..5. Offset 3 returns 2. Offset 1 returns 1. Offset 10 returns 0. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: view::tests::fold_covering_count_counts_every_range
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because fold_covering_count does not exist. For a, newline, two spaces, b, newline, offsets 0 and 6 return 0 and offsets 1 and 5 return 1. With ranges 0..10 and 2..5, offset 3 returns 2 and offset 10 returns 0.
